note: new trait: ommatidia_count (key already in use on main; millipede counts are filed there, e.g. Caucaseuma strasseri, and a right/left pair as one record in the form of Syrbatus obsidian, desk-d311). Paper's name Pseudonannolene canastra Gallo & Bichuette, 2020. Name (audit 473): Iniesta LFM, Bouzan RS, Brescovit AD 2023, European Journal of Taxonomy 867: 1-312 (10.5852/ejt.2023.867.2109, CC BY 4.0), abstract: 'The following taxa are synonymized: P. canastra Gallo & Bichuette, 2020 and P. saguassu Iniesta & Ferreira, 2013 with P. ambuatinga Iniesta & Ferreira, 2013'; same work places the genus in Spirostreptida, Pseudonannolenidae; MilliBase not reached. Discussion: the authors conclude the species does not have a reduced number of ommatidia, the family has 'four to 45 ommatidia' and they are 'rarely absent', the epigean Typhlonannolene adaptus lacks ommatidia, and 'it is difficult to infer if this character-state truly represents a troglomorphism.' The Methods give no counting procedure; the sentence cites Richter et al. 2010. Right 22 and left 24 are the paper's asymmetric counts; the eye area and lengths in the same sentence are not logged.
